target_customer: Brazilian online shoppers who want installments through Pix, plus e-commerce merchants who add Drip at checkout
problem: Brazilians lack an easy, low cost way to split online purchases into installments. Drip let customers pay in three monthly interest free installments over the Pix instant payment network, with 2 percent cashback.
business_model: BNPL over Pix; merchants pay a fee and the company extends short term credit to consumers
product_category: Buy now pay later via Pix

founders.name: Patrick McDougall Sterea
prior_employers: Nubank (Pix, e-commerce and open banking projects)

founders.name: Paulo Albuquerque
education: Fucapi, computer science degree and MBA in project management
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page; Bloomberg Linea confirms former Nubank.

founders.name: Bianca Orsini
education: Universidade de Brasilia, civil engineering bachelor's and master's in tunnel construction
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page. Bloomberg Linea names only the first two as founders.

exit.reason: Cash and share swap; founders left and all investors exited; price undisclosed

competitors.name: Pagaleve
competitors.what: Pix installment payments for online merchants in Brazil
competitors.traction_then: Not stated in the source beyond a US$25M round
competitors.funding_then: US$25M round led by Salesforce Ventures

technical_complexity.rationale: Credit risk decisioning, collections and integration with Pix and merchant checkouts, standard fintech engineering with credit risk the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Pix installment is replicable by banks and fintechs; the source on Pagaleve calls its risk engine its barrier to entry, which shows the moat is underwriting data, not the product.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Banks such as Itau offered installment options on Pix transfers per a search summary, and Pagaleve scaled with Salesforce backing. Drip was bought by Malga in December 2024 rather than copied out of existence.

market_need_then: The YC launch post criticizes high Brazilian credit card APRs and notes that Pix covers most e-commerce payments, so a credit product on Pix addressed an obvious gap. Pagaleve's US$25M round in September 2022 shows investor demand for the same wedge.

branding.domain_note: Uses dripapp.com.br, not an exact .com; the company is Drip Tecnologia LTDA of Sao Paulo.

identity.logo: not described in any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain Portuguese consumer copy: pay with Pix in three interest free installments with 2 percent cashback.

branding.brand_signature: Pix parcelado in 3x with 2 percent cashback
branding.community_and_virality: Brazilian business press covered the company (Startups.com.br, Finsiders Brasil, Startupi, Bloomberg Linea). Malga said the Drip brand would remain after acquisition. No merch or fan activity found.

brand_strength.rationale: A short evocative word, but shared with many other Drip companies, and no press about the brand itself beyond business coverage.

outcome_analysis: Drip raised a US$2.7M seed in 2021, a 2022 extension led by Costanoa and R$40M in September 2023 from SRM Ventures for its credit book, then sold to Malga in December 2024 for undisclosed terms with the founders leaving. Ex Nubank founders and Pix tailwinds helped it raise, while undisclosed price and founder exit suggest a soft outcome. YC marks it Inactive although it was acquired.
notes: Bloomberg Linea is internally inconsistent on dates (says Drip entered the market in 2022 but was accelerated by YC in 2021). It also lists an initial R$15M round with GFC, Possible Ventures and YC, undated; this may be the same money as the US$2.7M seed, so it is not recorded as a separate round. A search summary says the total reached US$6.5M after the 2022 Costanoa extension; that figure was not seen in the opened article, so the extension amount is left null. CB Insights total of US$8.41M and a R$100M valuation were seen only in aggregator snippets and are not recorded. The R$40M SRM round is labelled debt because Bloomberg Linea calls it credit funding; the Finsiders article says only R$40M investment, so the stage is uncertain. Pagaleve source is about 3 months after batch start. YC status Inactive conflicts with the acquisition; exit follows the press.
